instructions: Put the rice and 2 1/4 cups of water in a pot over high heat. Bring it to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on.
Drain the tofu and pat it dry with paper towels. Cut it into 1/2-inch slices.
Slice the mushrooms and the carrot thin. Cut the bell pepper into strips, trim the snow peas and mince the garlic.
In a small bowl, stir the cornstarch with 1 tbsp of water.
In a medium bowl, stir together the broth, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, salt and sesame oil.
Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat. Lay the tofu in a single layer and cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden. Add the garlic for the last 30 seconds.
Add the broth mix and the mushrooms. Bring it to a boil, then turn the heat to medium, cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Uncover and turn the heat to high. Add the carrot, snow peas and bell pepper and toss gently for 2 to 3 minutes, until they're crisp-tender.
Stir the cornstarch mix again and add it a little at a time, stirring gently. Cook for 1 minute, until the sauce coats the tofu.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Lead is Cup of Yum (5.0 from 34): tofu seared, then braised in a soy, Shaoxing and stock sauce with shiitake, finished with vegetables and a cornstarch slurry. The Plant Based Wok and Red House Spice versions braise tofu with chili bean paste for a Sichuan version. The optional oyster sauce is left out and the stock is vegetable, so it stays vegan. Tofu is browned a little longer than the source for a golden edge. Rice is added so the timeline includes it.
